key_phrases: higher volumes and a larger fleet is the right choice
harvest that margin in the future as we perfect autonomy
orders are in excess of production
the best service is no service
we'll be able to generate significant profit through autonomy
analysis.reasoning: The overall sentiment is cautiously optimistic, balanced between current margin compression due to price cuts and high confidence in future autonomy-driven profitability. Management shows extreme confidence (especially Musk) regarding the long-term moat provided by AI and data, while CFO Kirkhorn provides a grounded reality on current margin headwinds. Demand remains strong (orders > production), but pricing power is currently being sacrificed for volume and fleet expansion. The 'razor-and-blade' model shift toward software/autonomy is the central strategic pillar. QA was direct, though Musk occasionally used speculative language ('crystal ball') to deflect macro uncertainty.
